attachments.origin_landmark: oblique line of the mandible, between the symphysis and the mental foramen, deep to depressor anguli oris
attachments.insertion_landmark: skin and mucous membrane of the lower lip, blending with orbicularis oris and its fellow across the midline (the schema takes a bone id; the true attachment is cartilage/skin and is named in the landmark text)

actions: draws the lower lip downward and slightly laterally, everting it (expression of irony, doubt)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

fiber_architecture.evidence: no measured architecture recorded: no PCSA, fascicle length or force verified from a source for this muscle (Q65 rule: numbers only where a source gives them)

functional_compartments.function_note: Marginal mandibular nerve injury (parotid or submandibular surgery, facelift) paralyses it, giving the asymmetric lower-lip smile; the standard botulinum target for lower-lip asymmetry after contralateral nerve injury.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
